segments.body: New York City schools say they will explore other search options if Google does not change its position; Chicago has also reportedly warned it may look elsewhere. Google says it is working with educators and plans to make Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search off by default next year, so schools can choose which services to enable. The company is also piloting guided learning in Search.

Some educators worry about the effects of AI on students’ critical thinking, and the report notes concerns about children forming relationships with chatbots. But districts rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks and other services, making a full move away from the company difficult.

content.headline: Apple’s AI conversation recaps protect privacy but often miss context
content.shortHeadline: Apple’s AI recaps protect privacy but can misread conversations
content.standfirst: A two-week test of Siri Recap found safeguards that limit what the system stores, but also summaries that confused videos with personal conversations and stripped away attribution. The reviewer says the usefulness may not justify the social cost of ambient listening.

sources.originalTitle: I let Apple’s always-listening AI summarize my life for two weeks

segments.body: The Verge’s reviewer tested Siri Recap, an Apple Watch feature that listens to conversations and uses AI to produce summaries. It is opt-in; users can set when it runs, and recaps can expire after one, three or seven days. Apple says most processing happens locally, raw audio is not saved, and cloud processing uses Private Cloud Compute.

segments.title: When summaries lose the speaker
segments.body: The reviewer found that recaps sometimes treated audio from videos as personal events, and could omit the point a speaker considered important while preserving minor facts. With no transcript showing who said what, summaries of jokes or casual conversations could read as misleading or unsettling. The feature also has no outward recording indicator or audio chime.

The test found some work uses, such as recalling meeting topics, but little value in many personal situations. The reviewer argues that even a privacy-conscious design leaves users managing disclosure and explaining the device to people nearby. The reporting notes that ambient listening may suit straightforward situations where everyone consents, but it does not resolve the broader question of when recording is appropriate.

content.headline: Microsoft’s AI-first shift reshapes jobs as 60,000 employees offered buyouts
content.shortHeadline: Nadella says Microsoft buyouts reflect an AI-driven job redesign
content.standfirst: CEO Satya Nadella says the voluntary buyout offer is part of reorganising Microsoft around workers directing AI agents, not simply replacing software engineers. He acknowledges that the transition will be difficult for some employees.

sources.originalTitle: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit

segments.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says the company offered buyouts to 60,000 employees to give them agency as it reorganises around AI. He describes a future in which employees increasingly manage AI agents rather than doing each task directly, while saying the transition will take time and may be difficult.

segments.title: A new model of work
segments.body: Nadella pointed to a team of 11 developers building Cowork, an AI agent for Microsoft 365, as an example: he said they use AI to build the product rather than building it themselves. He argues that the approach will spread to other jobs, but his comments describe the company’s intended direction, not evidence that AI has already replaced those roles.

content.headline: Nadella says AI agents could force a rethink of the web’s business model
content.shortHeadline: AI agents could disrupt advertising-driven web businesses
content.standfirst: Microsoft’s CEO predicts that software agents acting for users could weaken business models built around human clicks and ad views. The shift could reward companies that let agents browse and transact, but the outcome remains uncertain.

sources.originalTitle: Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web

segments.body: Satya Nadella says AI agents could change how companies compete for traffic and sales online. If users rely on agents to search, compare and buy on their behalf, businesses built around people viewing ads and clicking links may need to shift towards transaction-based models.

Nadella pointed to Amazon’s decision to block AI agents from browsing and buying through its retail site. He suggested that competitors willing to allow agents could gain ground. The prediction reflects his view of a possible shift in the web’s economics, rather than an established outcome.

content.headline: England beat Australia by 97 runs to seal ODI series win
content.shortHeadline: England seal ODI series win with 97-run victory
content.standfirst: Ben Duckett’s 133 and four wickets from Sonny Baker powered England to a series-clinching win in Hobart. The result offers a boost as the side builds towards next year’s World Cup.

image.caption: England have won four ODI series this year.

sources.originalTitle: Duckett ton & impressive bowlers give England series win

segments.body: England beat Australia by 97 runs in the third one-day international in Hobart, sealing the series after recovering from a 131 all out in the opening match. Ben Duckett made 133 from 115 balls as England posted 328; Australia were dismissed for 231.

segments.title: A step forward
segments.body: New-ball bowler Sonny Baker took 4-45 after coming into the side for the first match, while Gus Atkinson again dismissed Travis Head in the opening over. BBC Sport said England’s series win was an important step towards next year’s World Cup, though dropped catches remained a concern.

content.headline: Bancroft's new claims deepen Australia's sandpaper scandal
content.shortHeadline: Bancroft's claims reopen Australia's sandpaper scandal
content.standfirst: Cameron Bancroft says players and staff knew about the ball-tampering plan in 2018, adding to claims from Usman Khawaja and others. Pat Cummins and several former team-mates have disputed or denied knowledge.

image.caption: Australia’s playing squad and staff before the third Test against South Africa in 2018.

sources.originalTitle: The sandpaper plot - who was there, who said what?

segments.body: In an account published by the West Australian, Cameron Bancroft alleges that Australia’s players and staff knew about the plan to use sandpaper during the 2018 South Africa tour. He says the substance was used in two Tests and that team discussions followed. Bancroft was the player caught tampering with the ball in Cape Town.

segments.title: Conflicting accounts
segments.body: Bancroft’s account supports Usman Khawaja’s claim that the team knew, and former player Chadd Sayers has also backed that account. Pat Cummins called Khawaja’s claims “100% wrong” and “utter nonsense”; Cummins and other bowlers have previously denied knowing of the plan. Former coach Darren Lehmann said he needed time to consider Bancroft’s allegations.

content.headline: Alcaraz reaches ATP Finals semi-finals despite hamstring concern
content.shortHeadline: Alcaraz reaches semi-finals with hamstring concern
content.standfirst: Carlos Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2 6-4 in Turin to reach the ATP Finals semi-finals and extend his winning run to 11 matches. He said he felt a problem in his hamstring after playing with heavy strapping.

image.caption: Carlos Alcaraz at last year’s ATP Finals, where he lost the final to Jannik Sinner.

sources.originalTitle: Alcaraz continues winning run despite injury concern

segments.body: Alcaraz controlled his match against world number five Daniil Medvedev, winning 6-2 6-4 in 72 minutes without facing a break point. His place in the semi-finals was confirmed after Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli.

segments.title: Fitness to watch
segments.body: The Spaniard said he felt “a little problem” with his hamstring and would consult his team and physio. The win was his 11th in a row, following titles in Vienna and Paris; he is scheduled to play Cobolli in his final group match on Friday.

content.headline: Pochettino starts Manchester United job with Liverpool trip looming
content.shortHeadline: Pochettino begins Man Utd job ahead of Liverpool trip
content.standfirst: Mauricio Pochettino has begun work as Manchester United manager after leaving the USA job, saying the club must be ready to compete at Liverpool on Sunday. United are 18th after winning once this season.

image.caption: Mauricio Pochettino’s first Premier League game as Chelsea manager was against Liverpool; his first Manchester United match is also against Liverpool.

sources.originalTitle: Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino

segments.body: Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday to begin a two-and-a-half-year contract. His first match in charge is Sunday’s trip to Liverpool, with United 18th in the Premier League and having won once this season.

segments.title: A rapid change
segments.body: The Argentine flew directly from the United States after his final game as USA manager, a 2-0 win over Haiti that secured a place in the Concacaf Nations League semi-finals. He said he had “plenty of energy” and wanted United ready to compete at Anfield.

content.headline: Premier League panel records joint-high six refereeing errors
content.shortHeadline: Panel records joint-high six Premier League errors
content.standfirst: The Key Match Incidents Panel says there were six incorrect on-field decisions in the latest Premier League round, equalling its highest weekend total. It unanimously judged VAR should have intervened over a hair-pull involving Everton’s James Tarkowski.

image.caption: The failure to award Arsenal a penalty was less controversial after the Gunners scored a second-half winner.

sources.originalTitle: Joint-record six referee errors in last Premier League weekend

segments.body: The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel recorded six incorrect on-field decisions in the latest round of matches, matching its highest total for a weekend. The panel reviews contentious incidents and separately considers the referee’s decision and whether VAR should have intervened.

segments.title: Everton incident
segments.body: The panel unanimously judged that James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi’s hair in the area and that VAR should have intervened. The report says the six errors include only two missed VAR interventions, underscoring the difference between a wrong on-field decision and one that meets the threshold for video review.

content.headline: FA considered legal challenge to Infantino's bid for a fourth term
content.shortHeadline: FA considered challenge to Infantino's fourth-term bid
content.standfirst: The Football Association says it considered challenging Gianni Infantino’s eligibility to seek a fourth term as Fifa president, but believes a case would probably fail. It is backing rival candidate Philippe Diallo.

image.caption: Gianni Infantino has led Fifa since 2016.

sources.originalTitle: FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on

segments.body: The FA explored whether it could challenge Infantino’s eligibility to stand in the March Fifa presidential election, but chair Debbie Hewitt told campaign group Fair Square that the body did not believe a challenge would succeed. Fifa’s council decided in 2022 that Infantino’s 2016-19 period in office would not count towards the term limit.

segments.title: The challenge to the FA’s position
segments.body: The FA says it opposes Infantino’s re-election and supports Philippe Diallo. Fair Square urged the FA not to abandon the matter, arguing that doing so could signal that Infantino can ignore the rules. Fifa has previously said its council unanimously agreed the earlier period did not count as a term.

content.headline: Juan Mata retires from playing aged 38
content.shortHeadline: Juan Mata retires from football aged 38
content.standfirst: The former Spain midfielder ends a playing career that included a World Cup, Euro 2012 and major trophies with Chelsea and Manchester United. Mata says he will continue to be involved in football.

image.caption: Juan Mata celebrates winning Euro 2012 with Spain.

sources.originalTitle: Former Spain midfielder Mata retires aged 38

segments.body: Juan Mata has announced his retirement from playing at 38. He made 41 appearances for Spain and was part of the team that won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012, scoring in the European Championship final against Italy.

segments.title: A decorated club career
segments.body: Mata won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup with Chelsea, where he was named the club’s player of the year in both full seasons he spent there. At Manchester United he scored 51 goals in 285 appearances and won the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup.

content.headline: Carla Ward close to Republic of Ireland deal before Poland play-off
content.shortHeadline: Ward close to new Ireland deal ahead of Poland play-off
content.standfirst: Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says she is close to agreeing a contract extension as she names her squad for the World Cup play-off final against Poland. Saoirse Noonan returns after an ankle injury.

image.caption: Carla Ward was appointed Republic of Ireland manager in January 2025.

sources.originalTitle: Ward close to new deal as Noonan returns to squad

segments.body: Ward says she wants to stay as Republic of Ireland manager and that she and the Football Association of Ireland are close to agreeing a contract extension. She was appointed in January 2025 and has led the side to Nations League promotion and its highest-ever Uefa ranking.

segments.title: Poland next
segments.body: Ireland face Poland for a place at the 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil, with the first leg in Gdansk on 1 December and the return in Dublin four days later. Saoirse Noonan returns to the squad after missing the play-off semi-final with an ankle injury.
